<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    At March&#160;10, 2009, we had approximately 2,322 holders of
    record of our common stock.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We have not declared or paid any dividends on our common stock,
    and our board of directors does not anticipate declaring or
    paying any cash dividends in the foreseeable future. We
    anticipate that all of our earnings, if any, and other cash
    resources will be retained to pay principal and interest on our
    debt, fund our business operations, and build cash reserves and
    will be available for other strategic opportunities that may
    develop. Future dividend policy will be subject to the
    discretion of our board of directors, and will be contingent
    upon our results of operations, financial position, cash flow,
    liquidity, capital expenditure plan and requirements, general
    business conditions, restrictions imposed by financing
    arrangements, if any, legal and regulatory restrictions on the
    payment of dividends and other factors that our Board of
    Directors deems relevant.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><U><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Stock
    Repurchase Programs</FONT></U></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In May 2006, the Board of Directors of the Company approved a
    $15&#160;million share repurchase program which expired in May
    2007. Under this program, the Company repurchased
    225,267&#160;shares at an aggregate cost of $2.8&#160;million
    during 2006. During 2007, the Company repurchased
    146,625&#160;shares at an aggregate cost of $1.9&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In August 2007, the Board of Directors of the Company approved a
    $30&#160;million share repurchase program which was due to
    expire on August&#160;22, 2009. Under this program, the Company
    repurchased 1.3&#160;million shares at an aggregate cost of
    $15.2&#160;million in 2007. During 2008, the Company repurchased
    1.5&#160;million shares at an aggregate cost of
    $14.9&#160;million fulfilling the remaining authority under the
    program.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On April&#160;11, 2008, the Board of Directors of the Company
    approved the repurchase of an additional $10&#160;million of
    common stock over a period ending no later than April&#160;15,
    2009. As of December&#160;31, 2008, the Company had repurchased
    approximately 554,000&#160;shares at an aggregate cost of
    $4.4&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 18pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On November&#160;25, 2002, we adopted a stock incentive plan
    (&#147;Stock Incentive Plan&#148;) which replaced the stock
    option plan previously in place. The Stock Incentive Plan, prior
    to the completion of the secondary stock offering on
    June&#160;25, 2004, authorized us to award our directors,
    officers, or other key employees or consultants as determined by
    a committee appointed by the Board of Directors, options to
    acquire and other equity incentives up to 353,333&#160;shares of
    common stock. With the completion of the secondary stock
    offering on June&#160;25, 2004, the total number of shares
    available for issuance under our stock incentive plan increased
    to 3,301,058&#160;shares. As of December&#160;31, 2008, we have
    issued options to acquire 981,332&#160;shares (537,501 of which
    were forfeited), 12,413&#160;shares of restricted stock (of
    which 4,719&#160;shares were withheld to satisfy tax
    obligations), 66,666&#160;shares of restricted stock units (of
    which 21,633 were withheld to satisfy tax obligations) and
    350,566&#160;shares of nonvested stock (of which 27,741 shares
    were forfeited and 18,246 of which were withheld to satisfy tax
    obligations).
</DIV>

    The following stock performance graph compares the cumulative
    total stockholder return of our common stock between
    December&#160;31, 2003 and December&#160;31, 2008, against the
    cumulative stockholder return during such period achieved by the
    Dow Jones US Hotels Index and the Dow Jones Wilshire 5000 Index.
    The graph assumes that $100 was invested on December&#160;31,
    2003 in each of the comparison indices and in our common stock.
    The chart is adjusted to reflect a 1 for 3 reverse stock split
    which was effective on April&#160;30, 2004.

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Selected
    Consolidated Financial Data</FONT></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We present, in the table below, selected financial data derived
    from our historical financial statements for the five years
    ended December&#160;31, 2008.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In addition, in accordance with generally accepted accounting
    principles, our results of operations distinguish between the
    results of operations of those properties which we plan to
    retain in our portfolio for the foreseeable future, referred to
    as continuing operations, and the results of operations of those
    properties which have been sold or have been identified for
    sale, referred to as discontinued operations. The historical
    income statements have been reclassified based on the assets
    sold or held for sale as of December&#160;31, 2008.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    You should read the financial data below in conjunction with
    &#147;Item&#160;7. Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of
    Financial Condition and Results of Operation&#148; and
    &#147;Item&#160;8. Financial Statements and Supplementary
    Data&#148; included in this
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">Form&#160;10-K.</FONT>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The income statement financial data for the years ended
    December&#160;31, 2008, December&#160;31, 2007, and
    December&#160;31, 2006, and selected balance sheet data for the
    years ended December&#160;31, 2008 and December&#160;31, 2007,
    were extracted from the audited financial statements included in
    this
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">Form&#160;10-K,</FONT>
    which commence on
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">page&#160;F-1.</FONT>
</DIV>

    consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. Also,
    the discussion which follows contains forward-looking statements
    which involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results could
    differ materially from those anticipated in these
    forward-looking statements as a result of various factors,
    including those discussed above under the caption &#147;Risk
    Factors.&#148;</I>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Executive
    Summary</FONT></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We are one of the largest independent owners and operators of
    full-service hotels in the United States in terms of our number
    of guest rooms according to Hotel Business. We are considered an
    independent owner and operator because we do not operate our
    hotels under our own name. We operate substantially all of our
    hotels under nationally recognized brands, such as &#147;Crowne
    Plaza,&#148;, &#147;Four Points by Sheraton&#148;,
    &#147;Hilton,&#148; &#147;Holiday Inn,&#148;
    &#147;Marriott,&#148; and &#147;Wyndham&#148;.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    As of March&#160;1, 2009, we operated 41 hotels with an
    aggregate of 7,578 rooms, located in 23&#160;states and Canada.
    Of the 41 hotels, 35 hotels, with an aggregate of 6,655 rooms,
    are held for use and the results of operations are classified in
    continuing operations, while 6 hotels, with an aggregate of 923
    rooms, are held for sale and the results of operations are
    classified in discontinued operations.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    As of December&#160;31, 2008, we had $332.6&#160;million of
    total mortgage obligations outstanding, including the current
    portion. This mortgage indebtedness is secured by interests in
    certain of our hotel properties. Approximately $128&#160;million
    of this mortgage debt is scheduled to mature in July 2009 and
    cannot be extended without the approval of the loan servicers,
    which extension has been requested but not yet granted. To
    address the pending maturities, we are also pursuing
    opportunities to refinance the maturing mortgage debt or to
    acquire new mortgage debt using currently unencumbered
    properties. To date, we have been unable to secure financing
    and, in light of the current credit markets generally and the
    real estate credit markets specifically, we expect it will
    remain difficult to refinance the mortgage debt prior to the
    July 2009 maturity date. We cannot currently predict whether our
    efforts to refinance or extend the maturing debt will be
    successful. See &#147;Item&#160;1A. Risk Factors&#148; for
    additional information.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Total assets decreased from $624.7&#160;million at
    December&#160;31, 2007 to $555.4&#160;million at
    December&#160;31, 2008. The reduction was primarily due to lower
    cash balances (approximately $34&#160;million) and lower book
    value of property and equipment due to hotels sold during 2008.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Long-term liabilities decreased from $355.7&#160;million at
    December&#160;31, 2007 to $194.8&#160;million at
    December&#160;31, 2008, mainly as a result of the
    reclassification of the maturing debt from long-term liabilities
    to current liabilities. In addition, the long-term liabilities
    associated with the assets that were reclassified to held for
    sale during 2008 were reclassified to Liabilities related to
    assets held for sale.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The consolidated statements of operations for discontinued

    results of operations for the 6 hotels that were held for sale

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The assets held for sale at December&#160;31, 2008 and
    December&#160;31, 2007 and the liabilities related to these
    assets are separately disclosed in the Consolidated Balance
    Sheets. Among other criteria, we classify an asset as held for
    sale if we expect to dispose of it within one year, we have
    initiated an active marketing plan to sell the asset at a
    reasonable price and it is unlikely that significant changes to
    the plan to sell the asset will be made. While we believe that
    the completion of these dispositions is probable, the sale of
    these assets is subject to market conditions and we cannot
    provide assurance that we will finalize the sale of all or any
    of these assets on favorable terms or at all. We believe that
    all of our held for sale assets as of December&#160;31, 2008
    remain properly classified in accordance with
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;144.

    Where the carrying values of the assets held for sale exceeded
    the estimated fair values, net of selling costs, we reduced the
    carrying values and recorded impairment charges. During the year
    ended December&#160;31, 2008, we recorded impairment charges of
    $10.8&#160;million on assets held for sale.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Our continuing operations reflect the results of operations of
    those hotels which we are likely to retain in our portfolio for
    the foreseeable future as well as those assets which do not
    currently meet the held for sale criteria of
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;144. We periodically evaluate the assets in
    our portfolio to ensure they continue to meet our performance
    objectives. Accordingly, from time to time, we could identify
    other assets for disposition.

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Critical
    Accounting Policies and Estimates</FONT></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Our financial statements are prepared in accordance with
    generally accepted accounting principles (&#147;GAAP&#148;). As
    we prepare our financial statements, we make estimates and
    assumptions which affect the reported amounts of assets and
    liabilities, disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at
    the date of the financial statements, and the reported amounts
    of revenues and expenses during the reporting period. Actual
    results could differ from our estimates.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    These financial statements have been prepared on a going concern
    basis, which contemplates the realization of assets and the
    satisfaction of liabilities in the normal course of business.
    However, as discussed in &#147;Item&#160;1A. Risk Factors&#148;,
    approximately $128&#160;million of outstanding mortgage debt is
    scheduled to mature in July 2009 and the current severe economic
    recession has negatively impacted our operating results, which
    affects operating cash flows as well as our ability to refinance
    the maturing indebtedness. In the absence of an extension,
    refinancing or repayment of the July 2009 debt, these factors
    raise substantial doubt as to our ability to continue as a going
    concern. We have engaged mortgage bankers to facilitate the
    refinancing process and to assist in negotiations with
    prospective lenders. Management is also negotiating to extend
    the maturing mortgage debt. However, management can provide no
    assurance that we will be able to refinance or extend the debt.
    The financial statements do not include any adjustments relating
    to the recoverability and classifications of recorded asset
    amounts or the amounts and classifications of liabilities or any
    other adjustments that may be necessary if we are unable to
    continue as a going concern.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    A summary of our significant accounting policies is included in
    Note&#160;1 of the notes to our consolidated financial
    statements. We consider the following to be our critical
    accounting policies and estimates:
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <I>Consolidation policy&#160;&#151; </I>All of our hotels are
    owned by operating subsidiaries. We consolidate the assets,
    liabilities and results of operations of those hotels where we
    own at least 50% of the voting equity interest and we exercise
    significant control. All of the subsidiaries are wholly-owned
    except for one joint venture, which meets the criteria for
    consolidation.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    When we consolidate a hotel in which we own less than 100% of
    the voting equity interest, we include the assets and
    liabilities of the hotel in our consolidated balance sheet. The
    third party interest in the net assets of the hotel is reported
    as minority interest on our consolidated balance sheet. In
    addition, our consolidated statement of operations reflects the
    full revenues and expenses of the hotel and the third party
    portion of the net income or loss is reported as minority
    interest in our consolidated statements of operations. If the
    loss applicable to the minority interest exceeds the
    minority&#146;s equity, we report the entire loss in our
    consolidated statement of operations.
</DIV>

    <BR>

<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="width: 87%; margin-left: 6%"><!-- BEGIN PAGE WIDTH -->

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <I>Deferral policy&#160;&#151; </I>We defer franchise
    application fees on the acquisition or renewal of a franchise as
    well as loan origination costs related to new or renewed loan
    financing arrangements. Deferrals relating to the acquisition or
    renewal of a franchise are amortized on a straight-line basis
    over the period of the franchise agreement. We amortize deferred
    financing costs over the term of the loan using the effective
    interest method. The effective interest method incorporates the
    present values of future cash outflows and the effective yield
    on the debt in determining the amortization of loan fees. At
    December&#160;31, 2008, these deferrals totaled
    $2.7&#160;million for our held for use hotels. If we were to
    write-off these expenses in the year of payment, our operating
    expenses in those years would be significantly higher and lower
    in other years covered in the related agreement.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <I>Asset impairment&#160;&#151; </I>We invest significantly in
    real estate assets. Property and equipment for our held for use
    assets represented 80.5% of the total assets on our consolidated
    balance sheet at December&#160;31, 2008. Accordingly, our policy
    on asset impairment is considered a critical accounting
    estimate. Management periodically evaluates our property and
    equipment to determine whether events or changes in
    circumstances indicate that a possible impairment in the
    carrying values of the assets has occurred. As part of this
    evaluation, and in accordance with SFAS&#160;No.&#160;144, we
    classify our properties into two categories: &#147;assets held
    for sale&#148; and &#147;assets held for use&#148;.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We consider an asset held for sale when the following criteria
    per SFAS&#160;No.&#160;144 are met:
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 4%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    1.&#160;Management commits to a plan to sell the asset;
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 4%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    2.&#160;The asset is available for immediate sale in its present
    condition;
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 4%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    3.&#160;An active marketing plan to sell the asset has been
    initiated at a reasonable price;
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 4%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    4.&#160;The sale of the asset is probable within one
    year;&#160;and
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 4%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    5.&#160;It is unlikely that significant changes to the plan to
    sell the asset will be made.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Upon designation of an asset as held for sale, we record the
    carrying value of the asset at the lower of its carrying value
    or its estimated fair value less estimated selling costs, and we
    cease depreciation of the asset. Management&#146;s estimate of
    the fair value of an asset is generally based on a number of
    factors, including letters of intent or other indications of
    value from prospective buyers, or, in the absence of such, the
    opinions of third-party brokers or appraisers. While management
    may consider one or more opinions or appraisals in arriving at
    an asset&#146;s estimated fair value, our estimate is ultimately
    based on management&#146;s determination and we remain
    responsible for the impact of the estimate on the financial
    statements. The estimated selling costs are generally based on
    our experience with similar asset sales. We record impairment
    charges and write down respective hotel assets if their carrying
    values exceed the estimated selling prices less costs to sell.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    With respect to assets held for use, we estimate the
    undiscounted cash flows to be generated by these assets. We then
    compare the estimated undiscounted cash flows for each hotel
    with their respective carrying values to determine if there are
    indicators of impairment. The carrying value of a long-lived
    asset is considered for impairment when the estimated
    undiscounted cash flows to be generated by the asset over its
    estimated useful life are less than the asset&#146;s carrying
    value. For those assets where there are indicators of
    impairment, we determine the estimated fair values of these
    assets by taking into consideration indicators of value
    including broker valuations or appraisals. While management may
    consider one or more opinions or appraisals in arriving at an
    asset&#146;s estimated fair value, our estimate is ultimately
    based on management&#146;s determination and we remain
    responsible for the impact of the estimate on the financial
    statements. The broker valuations of fair value normally use the
    &#147;cap rate&#148; approach of estimated cash flows, a
    &#147;per key&#148; approach or a &#147;room revenue
    multiplier&#148; approach for determining fair value. If the
    estimated fair value exceeds the asset&#146;s carrying value, no
    adjustment is generally recorded. Additionally, if an asset is
    replaced prior to the end of its useful life, the remaining net
    book value is recorded as an impairment loss.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <I>Accrual of self-insured obligations&#160;&#151; </I>We are
    self-insured up to certain amounts for employee medical,
    employee dental, property insurance, general liability
    insurance, personal injury claims, workers&#146; compensation,
    automobile liability and other coverages. We establish reserves
    for our estimates of the loss that we will ultimately incur on
    reported claims as well as estimates for claims that have been
    incurred but not yet reported. Our reserves, which are reflected
    in other accrued liabilities on our consolidated balance sheet,
    are based on actuarial valuations and our history of claims. Our
    actuaries incorporate historical loss experience and judgments
    about the present and
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    expected levels of costs per claim. Trends in actual experience
    are an important factor in the determination of these estimates.
    We believe that our estimated reserves for such claims are
    adequate; however, actual experience in claim frequency and
    amount could materially differ from our estimates and adversely
    affect our results of operations, cash flow, liquidity and
    financial condition. As of December&#160;31, 2008, our reserve

    $10.4&#160;million.

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Income
    Statement Overview</FONT></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The discussion below focuses primarily on our continuing
    operations. In the continuing operations discussions, we compare
    the results of operations for the last three years for the 35
    consolidated hotels that, as of December&#160;31, 2008, are
    classified as assets held for use.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Revenues</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We categorize our revenues into the following three categories:
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<TR>
    <TD width="4%"></TD>
    <TD width="2%"></TD>
    <TD width="94%"></TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    Rooms revenues&#160;&#151; derived from guest room rentals;
</TD>
</TR>


<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>


<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    Food and beverage revenues&#160;&#151; derived from hotel
    restaurants, room service, hotel catering and meeting room
    rentals;&#160;and
</TD>
</TR>


<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>


<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    Other revenues&#160;&#151; derived from guests&#146;
    long-distance telephone usage, laundry services, parking
    services, in-room movie services, vending machine commissions,
    leasing of hotel space and other miscellaneous revenues.
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Transient revenues, which accounted for approximately 69% of our
    2008 room revenues, are revenues derived from individual guests
    who stay only for brief periods of time without a long-term
    contract. Demand from groups made up approximately 24% of our
    2008 room revenues while our contract revenues (such as
    contracts with airlines for crew rooms) accounted for the
    remaining 7%.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We believe revenues in the hotel industry are best explained by
    the following key performance indicators:
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<TR>
    <TD width="4%"></TD>
    <TD width="2%"></TD>
    <TD width="94%"></TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    Occupancy&#160;&#151; computed by dividing total room nights
    sold by the total available room nights. To obtain available
    room nights for a particular period, we multiply the number of
    rooms in each hotel by the number of days the hotel was open;
</TD>
</TR>


<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>


<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    Average Daily Rate (ADR)&#160;&#151; computed by dividing total
    room revenues by total room nights sold;&#160;and
</TD>
</TR>


<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>


<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    Revenue per available room (RevPAR)&#160;&#151; computed by
    dividing total room revenues for a particular period by the
    total available room nights over the same period. Our
    calculation of total room revenues and the number of available
    rooms is adjusted, as appropriate, for the opening and closing
    of hotels in our portfolio. Our RevPAR can also be calculated by
    multiplying our occupancy for a particular period by our average
    daily rate over the same period.
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    These measures are influenced by a variety of factors including
    national, regional and local economic conditions, the degree of
    competition with other hotels in the area and changes in travel
    patterns. The demand for accommodations is also affected by
    normally recurring seasonal patterns and most of our hotels
    experience lower occupancy levels in the fall and winter months,
    November through February, which generally results in lower
    revenues, lower net income and less cash flow during these
    months.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Operating
    expenses</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Operating expenses fall into the following categories:
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<TR>

</TR>

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    Direct operating expenses&#160;&#151; these expenses tend to
    vary with available rooms and occupancy. However, hotel level
    expenses contain significant elements of fixed costs and,
    therefore, do not decline proportionately with revenues. Direct
    expenses are further categorized as follows:
</TD>
</TR>


<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

    <TD align="left">
    Rooms expenses&#160;&#151; expenses incurred in generating room
    revenues;
</TD>
</TR>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 6%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We use certain &#147;non-GAAP financial measures,&#148; which
    are measures of our historical financial performance that are
    not calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP, within the
    meaning of applicable SEC rules. For instance, we use the term
    direct operating contribution to mean revenues less direct
    operating expenses as presented in the consolidated statement of
    operations. We assess profitability by measuring changes in our
    direct operating contribution and direct operating contribution
    percentage, which is direct operating contribution as a
    percentage of the applicable revenue source. These measures
    assist management in distinguishing whether increases or
    decreases in revenues
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">and/or</FONT>
    expenses are due to growth or decline of operations or from
    other factors. We believe that direct operating contribution,
    when combined with the presentation of GAAP operating income,
    revenues and expenses, provide useful information to management.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Rooms revenues decreased $1.1&#160;million, or 0.6%, driven by a
    1.2% decrease in ADR, partly offset by a 0.3% rise in occupancy.
    The decline in rooms revenues was the result of deteriorating
    economic conditions. In spite of the challenging economic
    environment, we outperformed the U.S.&#160;lodging industry as a
    whole in 2008 as our RevPAR decreased 0.9%, compared to a
    decrease of 1.9% for the U.S.&#160;lodging industry, according
    to Smith Travel Research. This was achieved largely because of
    our planned strategic shift toward the contract segment of
    business in order to react to market conditions.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Food and beverage revenues decreased $1.5&#160;million, or 2.8%,
    driven by a decrease in our banquet revenues as businesses
    reduced their spending on conferences and other events. Other
    revenues grew $0.5&#160;million, or 6.6%, due largely to fees
    for canceled events.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Revenue growth was negatively impacted by displacement.
    Displacement refers to lost revenues and profits due to rooms
    being out of service as a result of renovation. Revenue
    considered &#147;displaced&#148; only when a hotel has sold all
    available rooms and denies additional reservations due to rooms
    out of service. We feel this method is conservative, as it does
    not include estimated &#147;soft&#148; displacement costs
    associated with a renovation. During a renovation, there is
    significant disruption of normal business operations. In many
    cases, renovations result in the relocation of front desk
    operations, restaurant and bar services, and meeting rooms. In
    addition, the construction activity itself can be disruptive to
    our guests. As a result, guests may depart earlier than planned
    due to the disruption caused by the renovation work, local
    customers or frequent guests may choose an alternative hotel
    during the renovation, and local groups may not solicit the
    hotel to house their groups during renovations. These
    &#147;soft&#148; displacement costs are difficult to quantify
    and are excluded from our displacement calculation. Total
    revenue displacement during the year ended December&#160;31,
    2008 for the eleven hotels under renovation was
    $2.1&#160;million. The largest amount of this displacement
    occurred at our former Holiday Inn Select DFW Airport hotel,
    which was converted to a Wyndham hotel and recently completed an
    extensive renovation. Total revenue displacement for the seven
    hotels under renovation during the year ended December&#160;31,
    2007 was $1.9&#160;million.
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <BR>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Rooms expenses increased $1.8&#160;million, or 3.9%. Room
    expenses on a cost per occupied room (&#147;POR&#148;) basis
    increased from $26.64 in 2007 to $27.41 in 2008, an increase of
    2.9%, primarily as a result of a $0.6&#160;million increase in
    employee medical costs and increased seasonal labor as the
    hotels reduced full-time employees and increased contractors to
    allow greater flexibility in managing labor costs.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Food and beverage expenses decreased $0.5&#160;million, or 1.3%,
    driven primarily by lower food and beverage revenues, partially
    offset by higher employee medical costs which increased
    $0.5&#160;million in 2008. Food and beverage direct operating
    contribution decreased $1.1&#160;million, or 5.9%.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Other expenses grew $0.3&#160;million, or 5.5%, while the
    related direct operating contribution rose $0.2&#160;million, an
    increase of 9.2%. In total, direct operating contribution
    decreased $3.7&#160;million, or 2.4%.
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <BR>
    34
</DIV><!-- END PAGE WIDTH -->

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Operating income decreased $12.1&#160;million in 2008.
    Impairment charges increased $7.8&#160;million due to a
    $4.8&#160;million impairment at the Crowne Plaza Worcester, MA
    and the write-off of assets that were replaced during our recent
    hotel renovations, including certain building improvements and
    furniture, fixtures and equipment. Our renovations were largely
    related to hotel conversion projects and required franchisor
    improvements. In addition, in 2007, we recorded casualty gains
    of $1.9&#160;million related to the settlement of a property
    damage claim at one of our hotels as compared to casualty losses
    of $1.1&#160;million in 2008 primarily related to hurricane
    damage sustained at one of our hotels. Excluding these items,
    operating income decreased $1.3&#160;million, or 7.4%. The
    remaining decrease was largely attributable to the decline in
    ADR.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Other hotel operating costs increased $1.3&#160;million, or
    1.9%. The increase is a result of the following:
</DIV>

    <TD width="4%"></TD>

    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    General and administrative costs increased $0.5&#160;million. As
    a percent of revenues, general and administrative expenses
    increased 30&#160;basis points in 2008 to 6.3%. The increase was
    due in large part to higher employee medical costs. In addition,
    we benefited from sales tax credits and bad debt recoveries in
    2007 that did not recur in 2008.
</TD>
</TR>


<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>


<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    Advertising and promotion costs decreased $0.3&#160;million, or
    2.3%, driven by cost containment initiatives.

<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

    Franchise fees increased $0.2&#160;million, or 1.0%, but
    remained relatively constant as a percentage of revenues.
</TD>
</TR>


<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>


<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    Repairs and maintenance expenses increased $0.7&#160;million, or
    6.8%, primarily as a result of increased automotive maintenance
    costs and higher medical costs. As a percentage of total
    revenues, repairs and maintenance costs increased 30&#160;basis
    points from 4.5% in 2007 to 4.8% in 2008.
</TD>
</TR>


<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

</TD>

    Utilities costs increased $0.5&#160;million, or 3.9%. This
    increase is driven largely by higher energy rates. As a
    percentage of total revenues, utilities costs increased
    30&#160;basis points to 5.5% in 2008.
</TD>

    $1.1&#160;million in 2008 and decreased 40&#160;basis points as
    a percentage of revenues, to 6.9%. The decrease was due largely
    to lower property insurance premiums and lower claims associated
    with our self-insurance programs for general liability and
    automobile coverage.

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Casualty (gains) losses, net represent costs related to
    hurricane and other property damage, offset by gains related to
    the final settlement of the related property damage claims. In
    2008, we incurred net losses of $1.1&#160;million almost
    entirely related to the damage at the Crowne Plaza Houston, TX,
    as a result of Hurricane Ike. In 2007, we recognized total net
    gains of $1.9&#160;million related to the settlement of a
    property damage claim at our Radisson New Orleans Airport hotel,
    which was damaged in 2005 by Hurricane Katrina.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In August 2007, we announced cost-reduction initiatives to
    improve future operating performance. These initiatives resulted
    in position eliminations in our corporate staff as well as
    reductions in hotel staff at certain locations. As a result, we
    incurred restructuring costs totaling $1.2&#160;million, which
    included severance and related costs. All of the terminations
    were completed and the related costs were paid as of
    December&#160;31, 2007.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Depreciation and amortization expenses increased
    $3.2&#160;million, or 11.0%, driven by the completion of several
    renovation projects in late 2007 and 2008. In accordance with
    generally accepted accounting principles, we begin recognizing
    depreciation expense when the asset is placed in service.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    During 2008, we recorded $9.5&#160;million of impairment losses
    related to assets held for use. Of this amount, $4.7 represented
    the write-off of assets that were replaced and had remaining
    book value. The remaining $4.8&#160;million represented the
    write-down of the Crowne Plaza Worcester, MA to its estimated
    fair value upon reclassification to held for use in accordance
    with SFAS&#160;No.&#160;144. In 2007, we recorded
    $1.6&#160;million of impairment losses related to the write-off
    of assets that were replaced but had remaining book value.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Rooms revenues increased $9.0&#160;million, or 5.2%, driven by a
    3.8% increase in ADR and a 1.2% increase in occupancy. Our
    RevPAR increased 5.0%, while RevPAR for the U.S.&#160;lodging
    industry increased 5.7%. Excluding hotels under renovation in
    both years, our RevPAR increased 6.9%.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Food and beverage revenues increased $5.3&#160;million, or
    10.6%, driven by the successful execution of initiatives to
    improve our food and beverage operations. Other revenues grew
    $0.7&#160;million, or 9.8%, largely as a result of new programs
    offered at our beachfront and resort hotels.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Revenue growth was negatively impacted by displacement. Total
    revenue displacement during the year ended December&#160;31,
    2007 for the seven hotels under renovation was
    $1.9&#160;million. The largest amount of this displacement
    occurred at our former Holiday Inn Select DFW Airport hotel,
    which was recently converted to a Wyndham hotel and is
    undergoing an extensive renovation. Total revenue displacement
    for the year ended December&#160;31, 2006 was $0.3&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Direct
    operating expenses&#160;&#151; Continuing Operations</FONT></I>
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <BR>
    37
</DIV><!-- END PAGE WIDTH -->
<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="width: 87%; margin-left: 6%"><!-- BEGIN PAGE WIDTH -->

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Rooms expenses increased $1.5&#160;million, or 3.5%. Room
    expenses on a cost per occupied room (&#147;POR&#148;) basis
    increased from $26.08 in 2006 to $26.64 in 2007, an increase of
    2.1%, primarily as a result of higher fee-based expenses
    including credit card and other commissions driven by revenue
    growth. Direct operating contribution for rooms increased
    $7.4&#160;million, a growth rate of 5.8%. The increase in direct
    operating contribution is attributable to the realization of our
    labor management initiatives.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Food and beverage expenses increased $2.4&#160;million, or 6.8%,
    driven primarily by higher food and beverage revenues. Food and
    beverage direct operating contribution grew $2.9&#160;million,
    or 19.4%, largely as a result of the successful deployment of
    our revenue growth and labor management initiatives.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Other expenses grew $0.1&#160;million, or 1.9%, while the
    related direct operating contribution rose $0.6&#160;million, an
    increase of 35.4%. In total, direct operating contribution
    increased $10.9&#160;million, or 7.6%. As a percentage of total
    revenues, direct operating contribution expanded 60&#160;basis
    points, from 63.3% to 63.9%.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Other
    operating expenses&#160;&#151; Continuing Operations</FONT></I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Other hotel operating costs increased $5.2&#160;million, or
    8.1%. The increase is a result of the following:
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<TR>
    <TD width="4%"></TD>
    <TD width="2%"></TD>
    <TD width="94%"></TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    General and administrative costs increased $1.6&#160;million. As
    a percent of revenues, general and administrative expenses
    increased 30&#160;basis points in 2007 to 6.0%. The increase was
    due in large part to higher payroll costs (fewer vacant
    positions and higher caliber employees), legal and other
    professional fees, relocation, and travel and training costs.
</TD>
</TR>


<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>


<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    Advertising and promotion costs increased $1.6&#160;million, or
    14.2%. As a percentage of revenues, advertising and promotional
    costs increased 30&#160;basis points from 5.0% in 2006 to 5.3%
    in 2007. The increase is largely attributable to staffing
    related to sales and marketing programs designed to drive higher
    revenues.
</TD>
</TR>


<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>


<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    Franchise fees increased $1.1&#160;million, or 6.9%, primarily
    as a result of revenue growth. As a percentage of revenues,
    franchise fees remained flat year over year at 7.0%.
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<TR>

    <TD width="2%"></TD>
    <TD width="94%"></TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    Repairs and maintenance expenses were essentially flat to the
    prior year, resulting from improved preventive maintenance
    programs and the execution of our capital expenditures plan. As
    a percentage of total revenues, repairs and maintenance costs
    decreased 30&#160;basis points from 4.8% in 2006 to 4.5% in 2007.
</TD>
</TR>


<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>


<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    Utilities costs increased $0.4&#160;million, or 3.5%. This
    increase is driven largely by higher occupancy. As a percentage
    of total revenues, utilities costs decreased 20&#160;basis
    points to 5.2% in 2007.
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Property and other taxes, insurance and leases increased
    $0.3&#160;million in 2007 and but decreased 30&#160;basis points
    as a percentage of revenues, to 7.3%. The increase was the
    result of higher claims associated with our self-insurance
    programs.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Corporate and other expenses increased $0.7&#160;million, or
    3.4%, due largely to the following:
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<TR>
    <TD width="4%"></TD>
    <TD width="2%"></TD>
    <TD width="94%"></TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    In January 2007, we announced a review of strategic alternatives
    to enhance shareholder value. During 2007, we incurred
    $1.5&#160;million in related costs. Similar costs were not
    incurred in 2006.
</TD>
</TR>


<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>


<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    $0.4&#160;million related to the amortization of non-vested
    stock awards granted to our Board of Directors in February 2007.
    Two members of the Board did not stand for reelection at the
    April 2007 annual meeting of stockholders. In addition, one
    Board member resigned in August 2007 and another Board member
    resigned in December 2007. The Board of Directors elected to
    accelerate the vesting of the awards for all four of these
    members and the related expense was recorded. The stock awarded
    to the remaining members of our Board of Directors is being
    amortized over a three-year vesting period at an annualized rate
    of $0.1&#160;million.
</TD>
</TR>


<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>


<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    These increases in costs were largely offset by lower payroll
    and related expenses primarily as a result of the August 2007
    restructuring plan.
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Casualty (gains) losses, net represent costs related to
    hurricane and other property damage, offset by gains related to
    the final settlement of the related property damage claims. In
    2007, we recognized total net gains of $1.9&#160;million related
    to the settlement of a property damage claim at our Radisson New
    Orleans Airport hotel, which was damaged in 2005 by Hurricane
    Katrina.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In August 2007, we announced cost-reduction initiatives to
    improve future operating performance. These initiatives resulted
    in position eliminations in our corporate and regional staff as
    well as reductions in hotel staff at certain locations. As a
    result, we incurred restructuring costs totaling
    $1.2&#160;million, which included severance and related costs.
    All of the terminations were completed and the related costs
    were paid as of December&#160;31, 2007.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Depreciation and amortization expenses increased
    $1.4&#160;million, or 4.9%, driven by the completion of several
    renovation projects in 2006 and 2007. In accordance with
    generally accepted accounting principles, we begin recognizing
    depreciation expense when the asset is placed in service.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    During 2007, we recorded $1.6&#160;million of impairment losses
    related to the write-off of assets that were replaced but had
    remaining book value.
</DIV>

<DIV style="width: 87%; margin-left: 6%"><!-- BEGIN PAGE WIDTH -->

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Interest expense increased $1.2&#160;million following the
    refinancing that occurred in April 2007. We entered into a
    $130&#160;million loan agreement with Goldman Sachs Commercial
    Mortgage Capital, L.P., defeased the entire $67.7&#160;million
    balance of the Merrill Lynch Fixed Rate&#160;#2 Loan, and paid
    off the $55.8&#160;million Merrill Lynch Floating Rate Loan. The
    refinancing decreased our overall interest expense, but resulted
    in higher interest expense for continuing operations and lower
    interest expense for discontinued operations based on the
    respective hotels that were encumbered by the debt facilities.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The $3.3&#160;million loss on debt extinguishment was a result
    of the April 2007 refinancing.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Results
    of Operations&#160;&#151; Discontinued Operations</FONT></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In January 2008, we reclassified an additional 9 hotels as held
    for sale. In May 2008, we reclassified the former Holiday Inn
    Marietta, GA to held for sale. In June 2008, we reclassified the
    Crowne Plaza Worcester, MA, from held for sale to held for use.
    As of December&#160;31, 2008, six hotels were held for sale.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In 2008, we finalized the casualty and business interruption
    claims for the former Holiday Inn Marietta, GA, which suffered a
    fire on January&#160;15, 2006. We received proceeds totaling
    $6.1&#160;million, of which $0.7&#160;million related to
    business interruption and $5.4&#160;million related to casualty
    claims. As a result of the settlement, we recognized business
    interruption insurance proceeds of $0.7&#160;million and a total
    casualty gain of $5.6&#160;million, after deducting related
    costs.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Income
    Taxes</FONT></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We expect to have a taxable loss of $3.4&#160;million for the
    year ended December&#160;31, 2008. We reported a net taxable
    loss of $49.5&#160;million for federal income tax purposes for
    the year ended December&#160;31, 2007. We reported taxable
    income for federal income tax purposes for the year ended
    December&#160;31, 2006. Because we have net operating losses
    (&#147;NOLs&#148;) available we paid no federal income taxes. At
    December&#160;31, 2008, we have available net operating loss
    carryforwards of $223.0&#160;million for federal income tax
    purposes, which will expire in years 2018 through 2028 if not
    utilized against taxable income. In addition, we have excess tax
    benefits related to current year stock option exercises
    subsequent to the adoption of FAS&#160;123(R) of
    $1.0&#160;million that are not recorded as a deferred tax asset
    as the amounts have not yet resulted in a reduction in current
    taxes payable. The benefit of these deductions will be recorded
    to additional paid-in capital at the time the tax deduction
    results in a reduction of current taxes payable. Our 2002
    reorganization under Chapter&#160;11 and our 2004 secondary
    stock offering resulted in &#147;ownership changes,&#148; as
    defined in Section&#160;382 of the Internal Revenue Code. As a
    result of the most recent Section&#160;382 ownership change, our
    ability to use these net operating loss carryforwards is subject
    to an annual limitation of $8.3&#160;million. Net operating loss
    carryforwards generated during the 2004 calendar year after
    June&#160;24, 2004 as well as those generated during the 2005
    and 2007 calendar year, are generally not subject to
    Section&#160;382 limitations to the extent the losses generated
    are not recognized built in losses. At the June&#160;24, 2004
    ownership change date we had a Net Unrealized Built in Loss
    (&#147;NUBIL&#148;) of $150&#160;million. As of
    December&#160;31, 2008, $95.7&#160;million of the NUBIL has been
    recognized. The amount of losses subject to Section&#160;382
    limitations is $171.5&#160;million; losses not subject to 382
    limitations are $51.5&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    At December&#160;31, 2008, a valuation allowance of
    $64.1&#160;million fully offset our net deferred tax asset. As a
    result of our history of losses, we believed it was more likely
    than not that our net deferred tax asset would not be realized
    and, therefore, provided a valuation allowance to fully reserve
    against these amounts. Of this $64.1&#160;million, the 2008
    deferred tax asset was increased by $4.9&#160;million with
    $6.0&#160;million of the increase relating to impairment charges
    incurred for books, $(0.6)&#160;million related to prior year
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">true-ups,</FONT>
    and by $(0.5)&#160;million of additional deferred tax assets
    generated during the period. The balance of $64.1&#160;million
    is primarily attributable to pre-emergence deferred tax assets
    and may be credited to additional paid-in capital in future
    periods.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In addition, we recognized an income tax provision of
    $0.1&#160;million for 2008, $1.0&#160;million for 2007, and
    $8.5&#160;million for 2006. $7.9&#160;million of the income tax
    provision for 2006 is for a non-cash charge related to the
    utilization of pre-emergence net operating losses in accordance
    with
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">SOP&#160;90-7</FONT>
    &#147;Financial Reporting by Entities in Reorganization under
    the Bankruptcy Code&#148;.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In July 2006, the FASB issued Interpretation 48
    (&#147;FIN&#160;48&#148;), &#147;Accounting for Uncertainty in
    Income Taxes,&#148; an interpretation of SFAS&#160;No.&#160;109,
    &#147;Accounting for Income Taxes&#148;. FIN&#160;48 clarifies
    the accounting for uncertainty in income taxes recognized in an
    enterprise&#146;s financial statements in accordance with
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;109. FIN&#160;48 applies to all tax positions
    accounted for in accordance with SFAS&#160;No.&#160;109 and
    requires a recognition threshold and measurement attribute for
    the financial statement recognition and measurement of a tax
    position taken, or expected to be taken, in an income tax
    return. Subsequent recognition, derecognition, and measurement
    is based on management&#146;s best judgment given the facts,
    circumstances and information available at the reporting date.
    FIN&#160;48 is effective for fiscal years beginning after
    December&#160;15, 2006.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We adopted the provisions of FIN&#160;48 with respect to all of
    our tax positions as of January&#160;1, 2007. While FIN&#160;48
    was effective on January&#160;1, 2007, the new standards apply
    to all open tax years. The only major tax jurisdiction in which
    we file income taxes is Federal. The tax years which are open
    for examination are calendar years ended 1998, 1999, 2000, 2001,
    2003 and 2004, due to losses generated that may be utilized in
    current or future filings. Additionally, the statutes of
    limitation for calendar years ended 2005, 2006 and 2007 and 2008
    remain open. We have no significant unrecognized tax benefits;
    therefore, the adoption of FIN&#160;48 had no impact on our
    financial statements. Additionally, no increases in unrecognized
    tax benefits are expected in the year 2008. Interest and
    penalties on unrecognized tax benefits will be classified as
    income tax expense if recorded in a future period.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In December 2007, the FASB issued SFAS&#160;No.&#160;141(R),
    &#147;Business Combinations&#148;
    (&#147;SFAS&#160;No.&#160;141(R)&#148;), which is a revision of
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;141 &#147;Business Combinations&#148;.
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;141(R) significantly changes the accounting
    for business combinations. Under this statement, an acquiring
    entity will be required to recognize all the assets acquired and
    liabilities assumed in a transaction at the acquisition-date
    fair value with limited exceptions. Additionally,
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;141(R) includes a substantial number of new
    disclosure requirements. SFAS&#160;No.&#160;141(R) applies
    prospectively to business combinations for which the acquisition
    date is on or after the beginning of the first annual reporting
    period beginning on or after December&#160;15, 2008. Earlier
    adoption is prohibited. We have $64.1&#160;million of deferred
    tax assets fully offset by a valuation allowance. The balance of
    the $64.1&#160;million is primarily attributable to
    pre-emergence deferred tax assets. If the reduction of the
    valuation allowance attributable to pre-emergence deferred tax
    assets occurs subsequent to the effective date for
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;141(R), such release will affect the income
    tax provision in the period of release.
</DIV>
