<TR style="line-height: 6pt; font-size: 1pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>


<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>    &#149;&#160;
</TD>
    <TD align="left">
    The Company is anticipating cure letters for two hotels to be
    delivered no later than February 2010.
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The corporate operations team, as well as each property&#146;s
    general manager and associates, have focused their efforts to
    cure each of these non-compliance or default issues through
    enhanced service and product improvements by the required cure
    date. The Company believes that it will cure the non-compliance
    and defaults for continuing operations hotels which the
    franchisors have given notice before the applicable termination
    dates, except for one hotel which is in default for failure to
    complete a Property Improvement Plan. The Company will continue
    to work with the franchisor to extend the default cure period,
    if necessary. The Company cannot provide assurance that it will
    be able to complete the action plans (which are estimated to
    cost approximately $2.5&#160;million for the capital
    improvements portion of the action plans of which
    $0.4&#160;million had been spent as of December&#160;31,
    2008)&#160;to cure the alleged instances of noncompliance and
    default prior to the specified termination dates or be granted
    additional time in which to cure any defaults or noncompliance.
    If a franchise agreement is terminated, the Company will select
    an alternative franchisor, operate the hotel independently of
    any franchisor or sell the hotel. However, terminating or
    changing the franchise affiliation of a hotel could require the
    Company to incur significant costs, including franchise
    termination payments and capital expenditures, and in certain
    circumstances could lead to acceleration of parts of
    indebtedness. This could materially and adversely affect the
    Company and its financial condition and results of operations.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Also, the Company&#146;s loan agreements generally prohibit a
    hotel from operating without a national franchise affiliation,
    and the loss of such an affiliation could trigger a default
    under one or more such agreements. The three hotels that are in
    default or non-compliance under their respective franchise
    agreements are part of the collateral security for an aggregate
    of $199.3&#160;million of mortgage debt as of March&#160;1, 2009.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    If a franchise agreement is terminated, the Company will select
    an alternative franchisor, operate the hotel independently of
    any franchisor or sell the hotel. However, terminating or
    changing the franchise affiliation of a hotel could require the
    Company to incur significant costs, including franchise
    termination payments and capital expenditures associated with
    the change of a brand. Moreover, the loss of a franchise
    agreement could have a material adverse effect upon the
    operations or the underlying value of the hotel covered by the
    franchise because of the loss of associated guest loyalty, name
    recognition, marketing support and centralized reservation
    systems provided by the franchisor. Loss of a franchise
    agreement may result in a default under, and acceleration of,
    the related mortgage debt.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    A single franchise agreement termination could materially and
    adversely affect the Company&#146;s revenues, cash flow and
    liquidity.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    To comply with the requirements of its franchisors and to
    improve its competitive position in individual markets, the
    Company plans to spend between $22 and $27&#160;million on its
    hotels in 2009, depending on the determined courses of action
    following our ongoing diligence and analysis. The Company spent
    $47.2&#160;million on capital expenditures during 2008.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Letters
    of Credit</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    As of December&#160;31, 2008, the Company had three irrevocable
    letters of credit totaling $5.0&#160;million which were fully
    collateralized by cash. The cash is classified as restricted
    cash in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets. The
    letters of credit serve as guarantee for self-insured losses and
    certain utility and liquor bonds and will expire in September
    2009, November 2009 and January 2010, but may be renewed beyond
    those dates.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 18pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Self-insurance</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company is self-insured up to certain limits with respect to
    employee medical, employee dental, property insurance, general
    liability insurance, personal injury claims, workers&#146;
    compensation and auto liability. The Company establishes
    liabilities for these self-insured obligations annually, based
    on actuarial valuations and its history of claims. If these
    claims escalate beyond the Company&#146;s expectations, this
    could have a negative impact on its future financial condition
    and results of operations. As of December&#160;31, 2008 and
    December&#160;31, 2007, the Company had accrued
    $10.4&#160;million and $12.2&#160;million, respectively, for
    these liabilities.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    There are other types of losses for which the Company cannot
    obtain insurance at all or at a reasonable cost, including
    losses caused by acts of war. If an uninsured loss or a loss
    that exceeds the Company&#146;s insurance limits were to occur,
    the Company could lose both the revenues generated from the
    affected hotel and the capital that it has invested. The Company
    also could be liable for any outstanding mortgage indebtedness
    or other obligations related to the hotel. Any such loss could
    materially and adversely affect the financial condition and
    results of operations.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company believes it maintains sufficient insurance coverage
    for the operation of the business.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Casualty
    gains (losses), net and business interruption
    insurance</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    All of the Company&#146;s hotels are covered by property
    casualty and business interruption insurance. The business
    interruption coverage begins on the date of closure and
    continues for six months following the opening date of the
    hotel, to cover the revenue
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">ramp-up</FONT>
    period. Management believes the Company has sufficient property
    and liability insurance coverage to reimburse the Company for
    the damage to the property, including coverage for business
    interruption, as well as to pay any claims that may be asserted
    against the Company by guests or others.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    With regard to property damage, the Company recognizes the
    related expenses as it incurs the charges. The Company writes
    off the net book value of the destroyed assets. As the combined
    expenses and net book value write-offs for each property exceed
    the insurance deductible, the Company records a receivable from
    the insurance carriers (up to the amount expected to be
    collected from the carriers). The casualty gain or loss is
    recorded upon final settlement of each insurance claim. Any
    funds received from the insurance carriers prior to the final
    settlement are recorded as insurance advances in the
    consolidated balance sheet.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    With regard to business interruption proceeds, the Company
    recognizes the income when the proceeds are received or when the
    proofs of loss are signed.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In 2004, several hotels were damaged by the hurricanes that made
    landfall in the Southeastern United States. In August 2005,
    Hurricane Katrina made landfall in the U.S.&#160;Gulf Cost
    region and two hotels in the New Orleans area were damaged. In
    October 2005, an underground water main ruptured underneath one
    hotel, causing flood damage in certain areas of the hotel and a
    limited amount of structural damage. And, in January 2006, one
    hotel suffered a fire. All of the hotels have since reopened,
    except the one that was damaged in January 2006 by a fire, which
    has been sold.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In August 2008, Hurricane Ike made landfall in the
    U.S.&#160;Gulf Coast region and the Crowne Plaza Houston, TX
    sustained some damage. Based on current estimates, the Company
    does not expect the total cost of the damage to exceed the
    deductible amount of $1.7&#160;million. As a result, the Company
    does not plan to file an insurance claim at this time.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In 2008, the Company finalized the casualty and business
    interruption claims for the former Holiday Inn Marietta, GA,
    which suffered a fire on January&#160;15, 2006. The Company
    received proceeds totaling $6.1&#160;million, of which
    $0.7&#160;million related to business interruption and
    $5.4&#160;million related to casualty claims. As a result of the
    settlement, the Company recognized business interruption
    insurance proceeds of $0.7&#160;million and a total casualty
    gain of approximately $5.6&#160;million, after deducting related
    costs. These amounts are included in income from discontinued
    operations in the Consolidated Statement of Operations.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In 2007, the Company recorded casualty gains (losses), net of
    related expenses, of $1.9&#160;million and business interruption
    proceeds of $0.6&#160;million in continuing operations, all of
    which was collected prior to December&#160;31,
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    From time to time, as the Company conducts its business, legal
    actions and claims are brought against it. The outcome of these
    matters is uncertain.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Management believes that the Company has adequate insurance
    protection to cover all pending litigation matters and that the
    resolution of these claims will not have a material adverse
    effect on the Company&#146;s results of operations or financial
    condition.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Operating

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    increases. The leases generally require the Company to pay the
    cost of repairs, insurance and real estate taxes. Lease expense
    for the non-cancelable ground, parking and other leases for the

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In August 2007, the Company announced cost-reduction initiatives
    to improve future operating performance. These initiatives
    resulted in position eliminations in the Company&#146;s
    corporate and regional operations staff as well as reductions in
    the hotel staff at certain locations. As a result, the Company
    recorded restructuring costs totaling $1.2&#160;million,
    representing severance and related costs. At December&#160;31,
    2007, all of the costs had been paid or otherwise settled. A
    reconciliation of the restructuring costs and the related
    liability is as follows (in thousands):

    Party Transaction</FONT></B>
</TD>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On May&#160;13, 2008, a Lodgian subsidiary acquired an interest
    in a ground lease related to the Holiday Inn in Glen Burnie,
    Maryland from WIH Hotels LLC (&#147;WIH&#148;) in an arm&#146;s
    length transaction. WIH is an affiliate of BRY/HY Funding LLC,
    which owns 6.1% of our common stock. WIH and BRY/HY Funding LLC
    are entities owned by funds managed by affiliates of The
    Blackstone Group. The purchase price of the interest in the
    ground lease was $600,000. The transaction was approved in
    advance by our Audit Committee pursuant to our Statement of
    Policy with Respect to Related Party Transactions.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On March&#160;4, 2009, the Company sold the Holiday Inn in East
    Hartford, CT for a gross sales price of $3.5&#160;million. In
    accordance with the terms of the agreement, the Company extended
    seller financing totaling $1.9&#160;million and paid
    $1.6&#160;million to acquire the land from the lessor.
